value: During exposure to appetizing and plain food cues in the food decision task, adolescents with excess weight, compared to those with normal weight, had increased activation in the dlPFC (bilaterally), superior temporal cortex (bilaterally), hippocampus, medial temporal cortex, putamen, superior frontal cortex, thalamus (bilaterally), globus pallidus, inferior temporal cortex, OFC, vlPFC, dorsal ACC, insula and dorsal caudate.
This pattern of activation suggests heightened reward valuation during preference formation and/or greater effort during action selection, two critical components of decision-making.

value: In participants with excess weight, “Appetizing vs. Plain Food Craving Ratings” positively correlated with activation in the dlPFC, vlPFC, ACC, insula, superior/medial/inferior temporal cortices, dorsal caudate, putamen and thalamus.
In contrast, only insula activation was correlated with “Appetizing vs. Plain Food Craving Ratings” in normal-weight participants.
These correlations support the general notion that excess-weight adolescents are hypersensitive to appetizing food cues.
